title: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4% to tackle higher inflation
summary: The Bank of England is raising interest rates for the first time in more than three years in an effort to tackle an inflation shock stoked by the Iran war
story: The Bank of England is raising interest rates for the first time in more than three years in an effort to tackle an inflation shock stoked by the Iran war

LONDON -- The Bank of England indicated Thursday that the sharp decline in energy prices after the U.S. midterm elections — if sustained — could limit the prospect of further interest rate hikes in the coming months.
After raising its main interest rate for the first time in more than three years to 4% from 3.75%, the bank said the outlook for U.K. borrowing costs largely hinges on what happens with the Iran war.

“We’ve seen encouraging news in the past 48 hours," Bank Gov. Andrew Bailey said at a press briefing following the first interest rate hike since August 2023. “The best thing that can happen is to resolve the conflict in the Middle East; there’s no question about it.”

The heavy losses suffered by the Republican Party in the U.S. midterm elections have been followed by a sharp drop in energy prices. Many believe that it’s now less likely that U.S. President Donald Trump will launch fresh strikes on Iran, with Democrats gaining control of Congress early next year following their big wins this week. Many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday, blamed the war for the party’s poor performance at the ballot box.
Though Brent crude is down around $15 a barrel this week, trading at $96, that is still more than $30 more expensive than it was at this time last year.

If the decline in oil and gas prices is sustained over the coming weeks, then the expected peak in inflation next summer — which the bank anticipates will reach 5% — could be lower. That could temper the need for future rate hikes, and not just by the Bank of England.

Other central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, have raised rates recently in response to the higher inflation stoked by the Iran war, and their interest rate strategies are largely contingent on what happens to energy prices.
Bailey said Thursday's hike “shouldn’t be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes” but stressed that the outlook depends on what happens in the war with Iran.
“Unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase,” he said.
For hard-pressed households facing higher mortgage rates and businesses paying more to access capital, the hope is that Thursday’s rate hike will be the last for some time.
“The path for interest rates is hanging in the balance, with U.S.-Iran hostilities holding the key," said Suren Thiru, ICAEW's chief economist.
The decision to raise interest rates was unanimous given the pickup in inflation this year, though one of the nine members of the Monetary Policy Committee backed an even bigger increase, to 4.25%.

The pressure on rate-setters has grown steadily in recent months. When inflation hit an 11-month high of 3.5% in September — well above the bank's 2% target — it cemented market expectations of a rate hike this month, with potentially more to come in 2027.

The main cause of the spike in inflation this year has been the sharp rise in fuel costs resulting from the Iran war and the ensuing bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz, which have squeezed global oil and gas supplies and pushed prices at the pump and household energy bills higher.
“There is now enough inflationary pressure in the pipeline caused by the rise in energy prices that an increase in Bank rate is warranted," Bailey said.
Interest rates in the U.K. had been trending downward from a 15-year high of 5.25% until the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

title: How one bank’s collapse is upending Paraguay, trapping savings and threatening its president
summary: The collapse of Ueno Bank has left savers scrambling for their money and Paraguay’s president facing calls for impeachment
story: The collapse of Ueno Bank has left savers scrambling for their money and Paraguay’s president facing calls for impeachment

ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay -- Hours after Paraguay’s central bank seized Ueno Bank, a major digital lender that went from an obscure finance company to a household name in less than five years, President Santiago Peña was facing impeachment, protesters were clashing with riot police and the bank's executives had been detained.
The swift collapse of a bank that claimed more than 60% of Paraguay’s adults as customers has sent shock waves through the country’s financial system.

By Thursday morning, a rebellion by several members of Peña's own conservative Colorado Party had become a party-wide revolt. Both of the ruling party’s main factions in the lower house pledged to back impeachment, with a debate scheduled for Thursday, after former President Horacio Cartes, the party’s powerful leader, withdrew his support for Peña.

Impeachment requires a two-thirds majority of lower house lawmakers present to send the case to the Senate, where another two-thirds vote would be needed to remove Peña, a 47-year-old former International Monetary Fund economist.

On Wednesday, before his own party turned against him, Peña had sought to move past the scandal in a video message, accepting no blame and promising to protect depositors’ savings. He also approved emergency payouts to depositors Wednesday and named a new central bank chief.
“Paraguay needs institutions that provide answers and protect our people’s resources,” he said.

The political upheaval and promises of relief leave a bigger question unanswered: how a bank linked to the president, who until last year had a stake in Ueno’s holding company, could grow so rapidly in size and importance despite repeated warnings about its dubious lending practices.

For many Paraguayans, the answer lies in the uncomfortable proximity of Peña’s long-ruling Colorado Party to the country’s regulators and business elite, a weakness that has endured even as steady economic management and rapid growth made Paraguay a darling of international investors in recent years.
“Santiago Peña and the Colorado Party have stolen all our savings,” said Luis Pineda, one of the protesters marching to Congress on Wednesday. “We are fed up with 70 years of plunder.”

Soon after winning its banking license in 2023, Ueno seemed to be everywhere in Paraguay. The digital lender, a rebranded version of a decades-old finance company, lured customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries, grew to more than 70 locations, sponsored Paraguay's national soccer team and plastered its name on the country's main stadium.

Government money poured into Ueno’s coffers under Peña. He also appointed Carlos Carvallo, president of Financiera Ueno, the predecessor to Ueno Bank, to run the central bank, the agency charged with supervising the digital lender.

As of last month, Ueno reported holding roughly $800 million in public deposits, about a quarter of its total, including money from the state pension and health fund and the operators of Paraguay’s giant hydroelectric dams.

Even as retirees’ savings and other public money piled up at Ueno, worries were escalating inside the central bank. In June, its inspectors found a pattern of risky lending to insiders, reported ABC Color, a leading Paraguayan newspaper. Ueno had extended large sums to companies tied to its owners, beyond what the law allows and without enough collateral to cover the debts if they went bad. On a single day in September 2025, nearly $39 million had gone to three such companies.
Peña repeatedly brushed off the warnings. As recently as last month, he defended Ueno and the central bank’s oversight, dismissing the concerns as a smear campaign that was spooking the public.

But on Monday, it all came crashing down. Regulators investigating Ueno’s loans to companies linked to its owners found poorly documented lending, the central bank said, as well as expenses the bank had wrongly counted as assets.

Once the books were corrected, Ueno’s capital, the cushion banks must keep to absorb losses, fell to less than half the legal minimum. The central bank seized the lender Tuesday and announced plans to move customers’ accounts, along with whatever assets still hold value, to other banks before liquidating what’s left.

Ueno’s app, cards and transfers went dark and its branches locked their doors, leaving desperate depositors lined up outside with no way to cash out their savings. On Wednesday, a rush to open new accounts elsewhere crashed other banks’ mobile apps, fueling public panic.
Officials appealed for calm and said they had begun repaying depositors, opening new accounts elsewhere for about 280,000 who had banked only with Ueno.
“The banking system is sound,” insisted Pedro Acosta Bernal, appointed interim central bank president Wednesday after Carvallo resigned at Peña’s request.

Authorities have detained eight senior Ueno executives, including founder Miguel Vázquez and bank President Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud. Lawyers for several of the detained said they needed time to review the allegations before they could comment.

Hundreds of employees of Ueno Bank and other companies belonging to Grupo Vázquez, the bank’s parent conglomerate, protested outside the Labor Ministry on Thursday, demanding severance and unpaid wages with their jobs in limbo and their salaries trapped at the failed bank. A day earlier, hundreds of retirees, depositors, university students and workers flooded the streets of Asunción, the capital.

“We want your head, Peña!” they shouted. Their signs demanded Peña’s impeachment, called him “the enemy of savers” and pleaded “Give us back our money.” Riot police fired pepper spray and rubber pellets to push back the crowds.

Many demonstrators saw Ueno’s collapse not just as the result of risky banking but as a case study in official corruption. Only Venezuela ranks worse in South America on the latest index of perceived corruption from Transparency International, a global watchdog.
“This is yet another assault on honest, hard-working citizens, people whose small savings are the fruit of years of labor,” said protester Belarmino Balbuena.
At the national stadium that once bore Ueno’s name, the bank’s logo had already been scrubbed away. But across the capital, fresh graffiti denounced politicians as thieves.
DeBre reported from Buenos Aires, Argentina.

title: Jaguars go all in to make a Super Bowl run with a flurry of moves, more NFL trades expected
summary: The Jaguars loaded up to make a run in the AFC
story: The Jaguars loaded up to make a run in the AFC
The Jaguars loaded up to make a run in the AFC. The Bears got an immediate impact from Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks, 49ers and Lions bolstered their teams.
Several significant players have already changed uniforms. More moves are expected before the NFL’s trade deadline Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

Everyone is watching the Minnesota Vikings (6-2) and wondering what they’ll do after Carson Wentz’s dismal performance against Buffalo on Monday night. The Vikings have to be calling teams looking for an upgrade at quarterback. Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and the offense has been mediocre with him. Wentz played well in Week 1 filling in for Murray and won his next start but he got pulled for Max Brosmer in a 23-6 loss to the Bills.
Would Las Vegas consider sending Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota? The Raiders (4-5) aren’t going anywhere and have Fernando Mendoza waiting but it takes two teams to make a trade.
Mac Jones is too valuable as a backup to Brock Purdy so it’s unlikely the San Francisco 49ers (7-1) would move him.

Daniel Jones finished the 2024 season in Minnesota so he’s familiar with Kevin O’Connell’s offense. The Indianapolis Colts already sent guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco in separate trades on Oct. 27. Running back Jonathan Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs and Jones could be next to go.
Jacoby Brissett was traded from Arizona to Baltimore last week after Lamar Jackson went down with a thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley sustained a season-ending toe injury.

Jacksonville went all in on Monday, acquiring defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III. The Jaguars (6-2) sent a 2027 first-round draft pick and a 2029 second-rounder to Philadelphia for Davis. They gave up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to get Bates from Atlanta, and a 2028 sixth-rounder that could be elevated to a 2027 sixth-rounder went to New Orleans for Godchaux.
That’s a lot of draft capital but the Jaguars lead the AFC South and are aiming for the No. 1 seed.
Detroit strengthened a depleted secondary on Monday, adding safety Andre Cisco from the Jets for a 2028 sixth-rounder.

Chicago gave up a slew of picks to get Simmons from Tennessee two weeks ago. The Titans got 2027 and 2028 first-round picks in addition to a 2027 fourth-round selection, while Chicago got a 2028 fifth-round pick in the deal. Simmons, an All-Pro defensive tackle, has been dominant in his first two games with his new team.
AP Pro Football Writer Mark Long contributed.

title: McIlroy says DeChambeau brings eyeballs to golf. To be determined is where he is seen
summary: Rory McIlroy once described Bryson DeChambeau as performative
story: Rory McIlroy once described Bryson DeChambeau as performative
What came across as criticism in July sounded a lot more like a compliment Tuesday when Rory McIlroy contemplated the nebulous future of Bryson DeChambeau.

DeChambeau was theatrical as ever when he protested a two-shot penalty for improving the path of his swing while stomping around in waist-high grass at the British Open. There were questions whether he would withdraw and rumors he was planning to call President Donald Trump. It led to players having to wait until nearly midnight to get Saturday tee times.
“I think a lot of it is performative,” McIlroy said at Royal Birkdale, making clear he was not a big fan of DeChambeau.
And now? DeChambeau is searching for a new home after the demise of LIV Golf, which on Tuesday in New Jersey filed a joint Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan.

The PGA Tour typically has a one-year ban of players dating to their most recent LIV Golf appearance, which could be longer if there are other disciplinary considerations (such as DeChambeau being part of the antitrust lawsuit against the tour).

He has the option of joining the European tour from winning a major in the last five years. That was the 2024 U.S. Open at Pinehurst No. 2 when he got up-and-down with a 55-yard bunker shot to win by one over McIlroy, who peeled out of the parking lot without a word.

DeChambeau already was planning to play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa, which the European tour co-sanctions, on Dec. 4-7. He has until Sunday to inform the European tour whether he wants to take up membership.
It's that “performative” nature that makes McIlroy believe DeChambeau would be a positive addition to the European tour.

“I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments,” McIlroy said at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

“And honestly — look, I’m certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be — but it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options,” McIlroy said. “If he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.”

There's always YouTube, which has given DeChambeau plenty of eyeballs. He has more than 3 million subscribers. DeChambeau has suggested he could devote time to YouTube and play the four majors, though it's always hard to tell if he's serious.

In his first public comments since the breakaway golf league announced it would shutter rather than launch a new version, DeChambeau in a social media post Sunday expressed no regrets for his last four years on LIV Golf and offered no clear details what was next for him.
He also invoked Arnold Palmer in saying the golf universe doesn't revolve around him.

“Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that along the way, I’ve said some things that didn’t help,” DeChambeau wrote in Sunday’s post. “Whatever comes next, I’ll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me.”

It was Palmer who single-handedly put an end to Greg Norman's attempt to start a World Golf Tour in 1994, a separate league with big prize money for only the elite players. Palmer said at a players meeting that he didn't like the idea, and the plan lost support. That was one of many reasons Palmer was known as The King.
DeChambeau only said of his future, “I'll go about whatever is next the right way.” He also said he thought there was still a place in golf for team golf, even if it doesn't include his Crushers.

DeChambeau was picked for the last Ryder Cup team at Bethpage Black in 2025, and he was performative and had eyeballs on him, just not many points. He won only one of the five matches he played, though he made a hellacious comeback to halve his singles match.

Are those eyeballs important for the U.S. team in Ireland next September? They might be considered more additive than valuable for a PGA Tour that already has the cream of golf minus a few players from LIV, DeChambeau and Rahm among them.

DeChambeau won five times on LIV Golf, one of those wins when he shot 58 in the final round at The Greenbrier. The limited schedule hasn't appeared to have any effect on his performance in the majors. Along with winning another U.S. Open, he finished one behind at the 2024 PGA Championship, played in the final group when McIlroy won the 2025 Masters and was runner-up to Scottie Scheffler in the PGA Championship at Quail Hollow.

This year was a setback — missed cuts in three straight majors — until Royal Birkdale. The penalty took him out of the final group on Saturday. A lost ball for a triple bogey took him out of contention for good. He was high-fiving and engaging the crowd through it all.
Performative? Yes. Eyeballs? Most definitely. The stage? Still to be determined.

title: Durant and Sengun power the Rockets past the Nuggets 110-100 to snap a 2-game skid
summary: Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets and snap a two-game skid
story: Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets and snap a two-game skid
HOUSTON -- Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday night that snapped a two-game skid.

Denver's Jamal Murray made two free throws to cut the lead to six points with about five minutes left. But Christian Braun missed a pair of free throws after that and Houston got baskets from Sengun and Amen Thompson to push the lead to 100-90 with four minutes remaining.
The Rockets got back on track after losing to Minnesota and Phoenix following a 7-1 start to the season.
Murray had 38 points in his fourth game this season with at least 34 points as Denver’s two-game winning streak ended. Nikola Jokic added 25 points and had 16 rebounds and eight assists.
Four quick points by Murray, with the help of a turnover by Sengun, got the Nuggets within four points with less than seven minutes to go.
But a short basket by Sengun followed by a 3-pointer from Fred VanVleet extended Houston’s lead to 96-87 with 5 1/2 minutes remaining.
The Rockets had a 16-point lead early in the third quarter before the Nuggets used an 18-2 run to tie it at 60-60 with about five minutes left in the quarter.

Jokic, Murray and Cameron Johnson all made 3-pointers to power that run while the Rockets missed nine consecutive shots and had two turnovers. Their only points in that stretch came on a pair of free throws by Durant.
Houston got its first field goal in more than 6 1/2 minutes on a basket by Tari Eason with about four minutes left in the third. That was the start of an 11-2 run that made it 71-62.
Denver visits the Grizzlies on Wednesday night.
The Rockets host Golden State Wednesday night.

title: Josh Allen and the Bills move to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the sputtering Vikings
summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills have beaten the Vikings 23-6 and sent Minnesota deeper into its offensive slump
story: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills have beaten the Vikings 23-6 and sent Minnesota deeper into its offensive slump

MINNEAPOLIS -- Josh Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before halftime, James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and the Buffalo Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into their unrelenting offensive slump.

Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams had interceptions and Tyler Bass made three field goals to stretch his franchise-record streak to 24 straight as the Bills (7-1) matched their best eight-game start since 1993. That season ended with their last of four straight Super Bowl losses.

With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz started at quarterback for the Vikings (6-2) and didn't finish what became one of the worst performances of his 11-year career. Wentz went 8 for 25 for 81 yards and three turnovers, including a backward pass in the first quarter that was thrown too high for even Justin Jefferson to catch it — resulting in a lost fumble near midfield.

Wentz, who was checked out in the medical tent at one point for an apparent lower leg injury, was replaced by Max Brosmer midway through the fourth quarter. Wentz completed 1 of 8 passes in the second half.
The battle of Buffalo's highest-scoring offense in the league against the least-scored-on defense might well have gone to Minnesota had the offense been able to muster a decent drive or two.
But the Vikings had four straight possessions in the first half start beyond their 40-yard line, and the furthest they made it was the Bills 48.

The Vikings as usual sent blitzers at Allen from every angle possible, recording four sacks and an interception of a heave into the end zone that Byron Murphy ran down and returned 55 yards. But the Bills eked out just enough in the first half to give themselves a cushion, when Allen found tight end Keleki Latu open in the back of the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown as he rolled right and was hit hard by Andrew Van Ginkel.

With 322 regular-season touchdowns — 232 passing, 88 rushing and two receiving — Allen tied Peyton Manning for the most in NFL history over a player's first 10 years. Allen is halfway through his ninth season.
Bills: Starting LT Dion Dawkins (ribs) and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were inactive.
Vikings: WR Jauan Jennings (calf) and FS Theo Jackson (quadriceps) were inactive.

title: Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski each score 25 as Warriors run away from Pelicans for 138-87 win
summary: Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87...
story: Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87...

SAN FRANCISCO -- Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87 victory Monday night.

Brandin Podziemski added 25 points while Curry wound up 6 for 10 with four 3-pointers coming off a 41-point performance in Saturday’s 126-119 overtime win against Orlando. He passed DeMar DeRozan (26,800) for 16th place on the NBA's career scoring list with 26,803.

Golden State had three players with at least 20 points for the second time this season and the Warriors finished with 30 or more assists — 37 — for the third straight game and fifth in the last six. They are 6-0 when doing so.
Injured guard Jimmy Butler dressed up like a member of the coaching staff and held a clipboard, writing “PASS TO STEPH” on it.

Derik Queen scored 16 points off the bench and Dejounte Murray added 12 points for the Pelicans, who were out of the game almost from the tipoff and trailed 72-43 at halftime on the way to losing a third straight after a four-game winning streak.

Golden State led 35-20 after one quarter as New Orleans shot just 7 of 23 and missed 10 of 12 3-point tries. The Warriors built a 23-point lead early in the second as Podziemski scored four quick points and rolled from there.
Charles Bassey contributed 12 points and 10 rebounds off the bench and De'Anthony Melton scored 16 with four 3s.
Lendeborg and Pelicans guard Jordan Poole, both former Michigan stars, traded jerseys afterward.
New Orleans rested Zion Williamson a night after a 139-123 road loss to the Clippers and Trey Murphy III also sat out to manage his troublesome knees after he scored 26 in Los Angeles on Sunday.

The Warriors lost second-year guard Will Richard to a torn ligament in his left thumb and the team said he would weigh his options over the next week on whether to have surgery or wear a splint while playing.
Pelicans: Host Brooklyn on Wednesday night.
Warriors: At Houston on Wednesday night.

title: Grayson Allen scores 27, Naz Reid adds 25 as Hornets beat Cavaliers 124-112 to snap 6-game skid
summary: Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 to snap a six-game losing streak
story: Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 to snap a six-game losing streak

CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 on Monday night to snap a six-game losing streak.
Tidjane Salaun added 14 points off the bench and Ryan Kalkbrenner had 15 rebounds for Charlotte, which shot 23 of 46 from 3-point range.
Charlotte built a 33-point lead in the third quarter then hung on to win after the Cavaliers cut the lead to 118-110 with four minutes left.
Meleek Thomas led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points.
The Hornets came into the game ranked second to last in the league in 3-point field goal percentage at 28.8%, but hit 12 of 24 from deep in the first half to build a 16-point halftime lead.
Allen, Reid and Salaun combined for 52 of Charlotte’s 69 points before the break.
Eager for their first win since Oct. 26, the Hornets stayed hot in the third quarter and extended the lead to 33 with Sion James knocking down three key 3s. He finished with 11.
Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson chose to play his reserves the entire fourth quarter even after his team trimmed the lead to single digits.
But the Cavaliers couldn't get any closer than eight and Royce O'Neale's 3 from the right wing with 2:40 left in the game pushed the lead to 13.
It was a big win for the Hornets. who played without starters Brandon Miller (hip strain), Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Moussa Diabate (quadriceps).
Peyton Watson added 13 points and Jared Allen had 12 for the Cavs. James Harden and Donovan Mitchell each had 11.

title: Luka Doncic powers the Lakers past the Hawks, stretching the win streak to 6
summary: Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night
story: Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night
ATLANTA -- Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night.
Walker Kessler had 21 points and 10 rebounds, and Collin Sexton had 18 points and six assists off the bench.
The Lakers were without guard Austin Reeves, who missed the game due to illness one day after scoring 43 points at Detroit.
Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 23 points and was 5 of 8 from 3-point range. The Lakers as a team shot 43% from beyond the arc (15 of 35).
CJ McCollum led the Hawks with 21 points off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 20 points and Oneka Okongwu had 16 for Atlanta, which saw its winning streak end at four games.
Dyson Daniels was the primary defender on Doncic, and he also had 10 points, eight assists, four steals and a rare 3-pointer.

The Hawks pulled cut the Lakers lead 115-111 on a Daniels bucket with 3:30 to play, but a 6-0 burst by the Los Angeles put the game out of reach. Doncic had a driving layup and an assist during the run.

The Lakers built a 20-point lead in the second quarter as they sliced through the Hawks defense repeatedly. Doncic set up teammates with eight first-half assists and Kessler had three easy alley-oop dunks off Sexton drives to the basket. The Hawks recovered late in the half with some improved shooting and cut the deficit to nine at the break.
Lakers rookie Cameron Carr had a two-handed dunk in transition in the first quarter for his first career points.

title: Lelevcius, Thompson score 21 apiece to send Clemson past North Dakota
summary: Liutauraus Lelevicius and Chase Thompson each scored 21 points and Ace Buckner scored 13 points and Clemson pulled away down the stretch to beat North Dakota 92-77
story: Liutauraus Lelevicius and Chase Thompson each scored 21 points and Ace Buckner scored 13 points and Clemson pulled away down the stretch to beat North Dakota 92-77

CLEMSON, S.C. -- Liutauras Lelevicius and Chase Thompson each scored 21 points, Ace Buckner scored 13 points and Clemson pulled away down the stretch to beat North Dakota 92-77 on Monday in the first-ever meeting between the two teams.
Thompson finished 9-of-10 shooting, making all three 3-point attempts, and Lelevicius made 9 of 9 from the foul line.
Dylan Faulkner added 12 points for Clemson (3-0). The Tigers shot 31 of 47 (66%), including 9 of 18 from deep.

Samuel Hincapie scored 22 points on 8-of-13 shooting, including 4 of 7 from 3-point range, for a spirited North Dakota (1-2) team. Luke Winkel scored 16 points and Zach Kraft 12. Kraft had three steals and North Dakota had 10 total.
North Dakota shot 28 of 62 (45%), including 13 of 27 (48%) from long range.
Not until Cole Certa made a 3 with 2:42 left did the Tigers record their first double-digit lead, 83-71.
Hincapie's 3 with 10:18 left gave North Dakota its last lead at 58-57.
North Dakota: hosts Montana on Saturday.
Clemson: hosts Georgetown Friday.

story: Xzayvier Brown scores 19 points to lead Oklahoma to an 81-72 victory over North Alabama

Mike Evbagharu scored 27 points on 10-of-11 shooting and grabbed eight rebounds for North Alabama (2-1). Quan Lax added 14 points and Jacobe Whitted chipped in with 13.
Evbagharu's layup to start the second half gave North Alabama its last lead, 38-37. The Lions led just one time in the first half when Caden Harris hit a 3-pointer with 1:07 left before the break.

title: Flyers hold off the Canucks 3-1 in a matchup of struggling squads

story: Michael Bunting and Travis Konecny scored in the first two periods to help the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-1 in a matchup of struggling teams

VANCOUVER, British Columbia -- Michael Bunting and Travis Konecny scored in the first two periods to help the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-1 on Monday night in a matchup of struggling teams.

Travis Sanheim added an empty-net goal for Philadelphia (5-10-5), and Christian Dvorak had two assists. Joseph Woll stopped 18 shots for the Flyers, who were coming off a 4-3 overtime loss Sunday night at Calgary. They had dropped three in a row (0-2-1) and six of seven (1-4-2).
Jonathan Lekkerimaki scored a power-play goal with 7:16 remaining for the Canucks (3-16-1), who have lost six consecutive games. They are 1-15-1 since a 2-1 start.
Vancouver continued to press after Lekkerimaki's goal but couldn’t find the equalizer. Leevi Merilainen finished with 14 saves.
The Canucks came within inches of tying it on a power play with 5:52 left, but Lekkerimaki’s shot pinged off the crossbar.
Sanheim's short-handed goal sealed it with 58.3 seconds to play. That was Philadelphia's first shot on goal in the third period.
Bunting returned to the lineup after sitting out five games as a healthy scratch. He skated on the top line alongside Dvorak and Owen Tippett.

story: Kyan Evans scores 26 points and grabs 10 rebounds for Minnesota, leading them to a 63-61 victory over Cincinnati on Monday night

CINCINNATI -- Kyan Evans scored 26 points and grabbed 10 rebounds for Minnesota, and Bobby Durkin hit a 3-pointer at the buzzer to cap the Golden Gophers' come-from-behind 63-61 victory over Cincinnati on Monday night.

Jaylen Crocker-Johnson hit a hookshot with 2:16 left, and Evans and Issac Asuma each followed with a layup during a 6-0 spurt to pull Minnesota to 61-60 with 14 seconds left. Cincinnati's Myles Colvin and MJ Collins then each missed the front on a 1-and-1.

Asuma grabbed the rebound off Collins' miss, dribbled a couple steps then lofted a pass across midcourt to Durkin, whose deep 3 found the bottom of the net. It was the Bearcats' first lead since 15:42 remaining in the second half.
Evans shot 11 of 19 and made three 3-pointers to go with five assists for Minnesota (3-0). Crocker-Johnson added 11 points and Asuma finished with 10.
Tylen Riley scored 16 of his 25 points in the second half for Cincinnati (2-1). Tyler Tejada added 10 points.
It was tied 30-all at the break and Cincinnati took the lead on Riley’s 3-pointer with 14:03 left, and the Bearcats had their largest lead, 49-41 with 8:12 to go.

title: Champions Classic: No. 2 Duke meets No. 5 Michigan State, No. 15 Kansas faces No. 24 Kentucky
summary: Duke, Michigan State, Kansas and Kentucky are gearing up for the Champions Classic on Tuesday night
story: Duke, Michigan State, Kansas and Kentucky are gearing up for the Champions Classic on Tuesday night
There were plenty of reasons for Duke, Michigan State, Kansas and Kentucky to load their exhibition slate with high-profile games.
This week is one of them.

The second-ranked Blue Devils meet the fifth-ranked Spartans while No. 15 Kansas plays No. 24 Kentucky on Tuesday night in the Champions Classic, this year hosted by the United Center in Chicago. For many years, the annual doubleheader represented the first big step up in competition for the quartet of bluebloods after easy exhibition games and lopsided regular-season openers.
That would have been the case this year, too, without those exhibitions.

Duke beat Army and Coastal Carolina last week; Michigan State blew out Quinnipiac and Toledo; Kansas handled Fordham and Middle Tennessee; and Kentucky took care of Manhattan and James Madison. The only game that was even close was the last of them, and the Wildcats pulled away from the Dukes in the closing minutes for a reasonably comfortable victory.

Compare that to the exhibitions they played: Kentucky faced No. 16 Texas Tech, Michigan State played UConn and Marquette, the Jayhawks played Louisville, Duke played Tennessee, and Kansas and the Blue Devils faced each other at Allen Fieldhouse.

“It’s part of the reason we played the exhibition schedule we did,” Duke coach Jon Scheyer acknowledged. “We wanted to be tested in different ways. There’s no question Michigan State is going to test us in ways we haven’t seen yet. We know it’s going to be a tough game but it’s also what we signed up for. We want to be in moments like this and games like this."
Scheyer just doesn't necessarily want that big moment to come without a little bit of work against similar competition.

Not to say that the slate of exhibition games is real competition. By design, they offered teams an opportunity to experiment with lineups and playing styles without any danger of a loss hurting their resumes. But after the Blue Devils beat the Jayhawks a couple of weeks ago, Scheyer admitted that the game felt nothing like a meaningless exhibition.
Now is when that pays off.

“I feel like this is a statement game for us just to show where we're at currently in the season,” the Wildcats' Zoom Diallo said. “Kansas is a premier college basketball team, and so are we. We're going into an atmosphere where we're ready to fight.”

Duke and Kansas are both 9-6 in the Champions Classic, which matches those same four teams in various combinations and different cities during the first couple of weeks each season. Kentucky and Michigan State are each 6-9 in the series.

“We're going to play a good team,” Jayhawks coach Bill Self said of their matchup with the Wildcats. “Two winningest programs of all time hooking up and playing at a neutral-site venue that'll, I'm sure, be turned up. It should be a lot of fun.”

The Champions Classic isn't the only big matchup Tuesday night, one of the few days of the week that isn't dominated by college football or the NFL at this time of year. Third-ranked Illinois is headed to Texas Tech for the kind of true nonconference road game that has become increasingly rare as schools chase NIL money available by playing neutral-site games.

Unless you're a prep football fan, Friday night is the other night that's relatively quiet when it comes to the pigskin. And that means the hardwood can take center stage. This week, Ohio State plays fourth-ranked UConn in Hartford, Connecticut; sixth-ranked Virginia visits Maryland; No. 12 Arizona heads to Auburn; and Seton Hall takes a trip to No. 18 Alabama.

The college basketball season really gets going next week, when the first of two Players Era Festival events takes place in Las Vegas, and a series of tantalizing nonconference matchups make for some prime midweek viewing.

In the “Players Era 8,” No. 1 Florida will face Notre Dame and No. 8 Houston will play Rutgers on Nov. 17 with the winners meeting in the semifinals. The Jayhawks will play UNLV and West Virginia will face Auburn with those winners also advancing.
The Illini, meanwhile, visit Duke on Nov. 17, the same day Michigan State visits Tennessee. UConn travels to Arizona the next day.

title: Bob Boone, World Series champion and part of 3-generation baseball family, has died. He was 78
summary: Bob Boone, the catcher on the Philadelphia Phillies’ first World Series championship team who won seven Gold Gloves and was part of baseball’s first three-generation family, has died
story: Bob Boone, the catcher on the Philadelphia Phillies’ first World Series championship team who won seven Gold Gloves and was part of baseball’s first three-generation family, has died

PHILADELPHIA -- Bob Boone, the catcher on the Philadelphia Phillies' first World Series championship team who won seven Gold Gloves and was part of baseball's first three-generation family, has died. He was 78.
Boone's son, Bret, announced his father's death Tuesday on social media. No cause of death was announced.
“He was a man of great integrity. He was a great dad, husband, and patriarch. It was a privilege to call him my father. Baseball lost a great one today,” Bret Boone wrote.
Boone spent his first 10 seasons with the Phillies, played seven with the California Angels and two with the Kansas City Royals. He also managed the Royals and Cincinnati Reds.

His father, Ray, played 13 seasons in the majors and was a two-time All-Star with the Detroit Tigers. Bob Boone's two sons both enjoyed long baseball careers. Aaron Boone played 13 seasons in the majors and played for the Reds when Bob managed the team. Aaron now manages the New York Yankees. Bret Boone was a three-time All-Star over a 14-year career spent largely with the Seattle Mariners. A third son played in the minor leagues. Bret's son, Jake Boone, works in the New York Mets' front office after playing at Princeton and briefly in the minors.

Bob Boone was a sixth-round draft pick as a third baseman out of Stanford in 1969. He was converted to catcher in the minor leagues and caught 1,095 games with Philadelphia, second on the Phillies’ all-time list to Red Dooin (1,124). Boone caught 2,225 games overall in 19 big league seasons.
He was the first Phillies catcher to win a Gold Glove (1978, 1979) and led the Phillies with a .412 batting average in their 1980 World Series win over the Kansas City Royals.

Boone made NL All-Star teams in 1976, 1978 and 1979. He set the record for career games caught by a catcher with 1,919 in Kansas City. He was 41 years old when he won his final Gold Glove with the Royals in 1989. Ivan Rodriguez and Carlton Fisk have since passed Boone on the career games caught list.

Boone caught the final out of the 1980 Game 6 clincher when Tug McGraw struck out Willie Wilson to win the World Series. Boone was involved in a more famous play earlier in that inning when he ran after Frank White's foul pop near the home dugout in Veteran's Stadium. The ball bounced off Boone's mitt and straight into Pete Rose's glove for an out — a catch played on countless highlight reels through the decades in Philadelphia.
He was added to the Phillies' Wall of Fame in 2005.

Boone won four more Gold Gloves, made another All-Star team and twice led the Angels to the playoffs. He went 10 for 22 (.455) with a homer and two RBIs against Boston in the 1986 American League Championship Series.
Boone went 371-444 overall as a manager, spending three seasons with the Royals and three with the Reds. He joined the Washington Nationals front office in 2005.
Washington won the World Series in 2019, the first championship in franchise history. Boone resigned in 2021 rather than comply with the organization’s COVID-19 vaccine mandate.

story: John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena
DETROIT -- John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena.
The Pistons overcame a 44-point, 13-rebound performance from Anthony Davis, who had been a game-time decision because of an ankle issue.

Daniss Jenkins finished with 22 points and eight assists after moving into the starting lineup. Jenkins scored a career-high 31 points in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers. Duncan Robinson scored 22 for Detroit.
AJ Dybantsa scored 21 points for Washington, which lost its fourth straight. Trae Young had 20 points and seven assists.
The Pistons led by 10 at the half and shot 63.2% from the floor in the third quarter. Jenkins had 13 points in the quarter as Detroit extended the lead to 103-87.
Cade Cunningham didn't return until midway through the fourth quarter after picking up a fifth personal foul in the third, but the Pistons had built a comfortable 115-99 lead.

Davis, who set the scoring record at the Palace of Auburn Hills with a career-high 59 points for the Pelicans in 2016, started the game like he was headed toward breaking Anthony Edwards' Little Caesars Arena record of 53.
He finished with 30 points in the first half on 10 of 11 shooting — making both of his 3-point attempts and 8 of 9 attempts from the free-throw line.
But he didn't get much help. Young scored 13 points in the half, but the other three starters combined for 14 points and the bench added just one point.
Meanwhile, the Pistons had three starters in double figures — Robinson, Collins and Cunningham — and got 19 points from the reserves.

story: Jason Crowe Jr. scored a career-high 34 points, setting Missouri’s single-game freshman scoring record as the Tigers routed SIU Edwardsville 96-58 on Monday night
COLUMBIA, Mo. -- Jason Crowe Jr. scored a career-high 34 points, setting Missouri’s single-game freshman scoring record as the Tigers routed SIU Edwardsville 96-58 on Monday night.

Crowe shot 11 of 16 from the field, made four 3-pointers and went 8 of 9 from the free-throw line for Missouri (2-1). The 6-foot-4 guard also finished with the most by a Tigers player since the 2023-24 season.

The performance was a sharp bounce back for Crowe, who shot 3 for 18 in Missouri’s 90-84 loss to Saint Louis. He scored from all three levels Monday, hitting from deep, knocking down midrange jumpers and finishing around the basket.
Crowe had 22 points by halftime as Missouri built a 48-24 lead. He reached 32 with 8:35 remaining on a four-point play to tie the freshman scoring record, then broke it with a layup with 4:02 left.
Toni Bryant added 18 points and seven rebounds for Missouri, while Bryson Tiller scored 11 and Jamier Jones had 10. The Tigers shot 58% from the field and made 12 of their 23 3-pointers.
Dehrio McCaskill led SIU Edwardsville (2-2) with 11 points.
Missouri forced 14 turnovers and held the Cougars to 17% shooting from 3-point range.
Missouri played nearly the entire game without Mark Mitchell, who left on the Tigers’ second possession with a facial injury and did not return.

PHOENIX -- Victor Wembanyama scored 40 points, grabbed 11 rebounds and blocked nine shots in another dominant performance to help the San Antonio Spurs beat the Phoenix Suns 122-96 on Monday night.
The Spurs have now won nine straight games after dropping their first two contests of the season.

The Suns had no answer for the 7-foot-4 Wembanyama, who controlled the game at both ends of the floor, particularly during the first half. The two-time All-Star had 22 points, six rebounds and five blocks before the break as the Spurs used a 21-2 run to take a 61-46 halftime advantage.

Dylan Harper scored 14 of his 17 points in the third quarter to help the Spurs extend their lead 93-68, which allowed the starters to sit for much of the fourth. Wembanyama finished 15 of 19 from the floor, including 2 of 3 from beyond the arc and needed just 25 minutes on the floor to do his damage.
De'Aaron Fox added 15 points while Julian Champagnie and Harrison Barnes both had 11.

It's the second time in four games that Wembanyama has had a massive stat line during an MVP-worthy run to start the regular season.
